title: A first for CRISPR: powerful prime editing alters DNA directly in the human body
note:
This really caught my eye: "But the FDA is expected to issue a decision early next year about an in vivo CRISPR–Cas9 therapy for a condition called hereditary angioedema, which causes severe swelling."

I am really excited about gene editing, but I do not know if now is the right time to build in the area since it is so freaking regulated. It seems to be that the science is moving so much faster than the regulation, and perhaps for the better, I don't have much of an opinion, but I've heard people talk about how the FDA has a process for the pre-AI era, and I am inclined to take it for face value. from a bio/acc stance, I think the counter argument to regulation is that 1) you have a moral imperative to speed things 2) something about DeSci and putting it on the blockchain??? sorry, again this is a place for me to think out loud I have a lot of weak spots in my knowledge, which is a good thing! lots to learn. 

So, in my case, I have a few options in my case if I want to build in gene editing:
1) Build and assume regulation will follow
2) Build in the infra space, which may be more favorable as a first time founder. I would have to think more about it for specifics, but perhaps create a product to sell to gene therapy companies. 
3) I need to dive deeper into it, but DeSci is a really interesting movement if I wanted to build in the regulation space. 
4) Build somewhere else
